result.summary:
RE-VALIDATION 4 (first pass on THIS diff -- prior three passes on this run covered the pre-transaction/INV-8 metadata work, which is unrelated; this is the first review of the M1/M6 update-only rework from REVIEWER's Step 2d OQ-5 FAIL). Read lib/letflow/event_store.ex and lib/letflow/event_store/instance_projection.ex fresh in full (not from memory of prior passes), plus `git show aac8f256 -- lib/letflow/event_store.ex` for the exact rework diff and `git diff aac8f256~1 aac8f256 --stat` to confirm the commit touches only event_store.ex (tenant_provisioning.ex untouched by this specific rework, already clean from the prior pass).

Scope test: unchanged from prior passes -- append/2 remains a tenant-data path (writes across events/instance_sequence/instance_projections/event_payload_store/event_idempotency, tenant_id derived from opts[:prefix]). IN SCOPE.

What changed in aac8f256: M1 (active_instance_guard/3) now returns `{:error, :instance_not_started}` on no-row instead of `{:ok, :new_instance}`, and returns the real `%InstanceProjection{}` struct (not a bare atom) on success. M6 (update_projection/3) replaced the insert_changeset/2 + on_conflict upsert with a plain `InstanceProjection.update_changeset/2` + `repo.update/2`, pattern-matching the struct out of `changes.active_instance_guard`.

INV-1 (tenant isolation) -- APPLIES, PASS. (a) Both M1's `repo.get(InstanceProjection, instance_id, prefix: schema_name)` (line 326) and M6's `repo.update(prefix: schema_name)` (line 521) pass `prefix: schema_name` -- confirmed by direct re-read, not assumed carried over. (b)/(c) tenant_id derivation: read `InstanceProjection.update_changeset/2` directly in lib/letflow/event_store/instance_projection.ex (not from ELIXIR-DEV's characterization) -- line 87: `cast(attrs, [:status, :last_event_seq])`. `:tenant_id` and `:instance_id` are absent from that cast list (the moduledoc at line 81-83 states this is deliberate: 'a projection never changes which instance or tenant it describes'), so even if `attrs` somehow carried a `:tenant_id` key, `cast/3` silently drops it -- structurally uncastable, not merely unused by this call site. update_projection/3's own `attrs` map (line 517: `%{status: projection.status, last_event_seq: assigned_sequence_number}`) doesn't even construct a `:tenant_id` key in the first place, so there are two independent layers (caller doesn't send it; schema can't cast it if sent) before this write path could ever misattribute a tenant_id. Row selection itself (`repo.get(InstanceProjection, instance_id, prefix: schema_name)`) can only ever resolve within the Postgres schema named by `schema_name` -- schema-per-tenant physical isolation per 0003 Dimension B -- so cross-tenant row access isn't reachable through this function regardless of the tenant_id column's cast status. INV-1 holds for M1/M6 specifically, not just asserted from the prior full-file pass.

INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 -- NOT-APPLICABLE, unchanged (no API/response-shaping code, no scripting sandbox, no lookup-by-ID endpoint; S4/S5 not started).

INV-4 (secrets) -- NOT-APPLICABLE, this diff touches no secret-resolving code (`grep -niE "password|secret|token|api_key|System.get_env" lib/letflow/event_store.ex` -- zero hits, unchanged from prior passes).

INV-6 -- APPLIES, satisfied by this handoff's explicit per-invariant statement.

INV-7 (no raw SQL) -- APPLIES, PASS. `grep -n "Repo\.query\|fragment(" lib/letflow/event_store.ex` -- zero hits (checked fresh against the current file, not just the diff hunk). M1/M6 use `repo.get/3` and `repo.update/2`, both parameterized Ecto.Repo calls; no raw SQL introduced or touched by aac8f256.

INV-8 (no unhandled crashes) -- APPLIES, PASS, specifically re-verified per the handoff's check (b): update_projection/3's pattern `%{assign_sequence: assigned_sequence_number, active_instance_guard: %InstanceProjection{} = projection}` extracted from Multi's `changes` map. Verified this cannot crash, not just asserted: (1) `build_multi/1` (lines 293-303) adds Multi steps via `|> Multi.run(...)` in a fixed textual order -- active_instance_guard first, assign_sequence second, ..., update_projection last (added after `maybe_store_oversized_payload/2`, which itself comes after insert_event). (2) Read Ecto.Multi's own vendored source at deps/ecto/lib/ecto/multi.ex directly (not from memory/training-data assumption) -- its moduledoc states plainly: 'all operations will be executed in the order they were added' and, on `run/3`'s contract: 'Returning an error will abort any further operations and make the Multi fail.' This is Ecto's own documented guarantee, confirmed against the actual dependency source present in this repo's deps/, not assumed. (3) active_instance_guard/3's only success return is `{:ok, projection}` where `projection` is bound from `%InstanceProjection{status: status} = projection` -- i.e. whenever it succeeds, `changes.active_instance_guard` is always a real `%InstanceProjection{}` struct, never an atom or other shape (both other branches, `nil` and terminal-status, are `{:error, ...}` and would have aborted the Multi before update_projection ever ran). (4) assign_sequence's only success return (via lock_and_increment_sequence/3) is `{:ok, assigned_sequence_number}`, an integer -- present under `:assign_sequence` whenever that step succeeded. Given (1)+(2), by the time update_projection/3 runs both active_instance_guard and assign_sequence have already succeeded and their result values are in `changes` with the exact keys/shapes update_projection/3's second argument pattern requires; given (3)+(4) those values are always the shapes the pattern expects. The pattern-match cannot fail on any realistic (or even adversarial) execution path through this Multi -- confirmed via Ecto's own documented short-circuit semantics plus this module's own return-value discipline, not asserted. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -- clean, exit 0. Heuristic grep `^\s*{:ok, .*} = ` in event_store.ex -- 1 hit (line 529), manually confirmed to be a `defp` function-clause head pattern match (`interpret_transaction_result({:ok, %{...}})`), not a bare raising assignment -- false positive, consistent with prior passes.

Overall: all applicable invariants (INV-1, INV-4 N/A, INV-6, INV-7, INV-8) PASS against the current M1/M6 update-only state. No FAIL manufactured to justify a fourth pass looking substantive -- the change is a genuine narrowing (fewer write paths, no upsert, no on_conflict branch to reason about) and every invariant this reviewer checked came back clean on direct re-verification, not inherited from an earlier PASS on a now-superseded version of this code.
